title: Offchain lending uses three LTV thresholds, and a margin call must restore the position all the way to Initial LTV
content:
Three separate ratios govern each offchain loan. **Initial LTV** (A.6.1.1.1.3.8.2.2.1.1) is "the maximum ratio of loan amount to collateral value permitted when a new loan is issued" — and does two more jobs: "when a margin call is triggered, the borrower must return the position to an LTV ratio **equal or less than the Initial LTV**," and collateral may only be withdrawn if the position stays below it afterwards. **Maintenance LTV** (.1.2) is the level "above which a margin call is triggered." **Liquidation LTV** (.1.3) is the level "above which a position may be liquidated immediately."

For BTC the ladder is 80% / 85% / 90%; for ETH 70% / 85% / 90%; for XRP and HYPE 60% / 70% / 80% (A.6.1.1.1.3.8.2.2.2.1 through .2.5).

The over-correction requirement is the design's most important feature. If curing a call only required dropping back below the *maintenance* level, a borrower at 85.1% could post a token amount of collateral, return to 84.9%, and be called again on the next tick — an oscillation that consumes operational attention indefinitely and leaves the position permanently at the edge. Forcing a return to Initial LTV rebuilds the whole buffer, so each call is resolved once.

The ETH ladder shows the buffers being tuned independently: a 15-point gap between initial and maintenance versus BTC's 5, meaning ETH borrowers get more room to move before being called but the same 90% liquidation line. Initial LTV governs how much leverage is *offered*; the maintenance gap governs how often borrowers are *disturbed*; the liquidation line governs when Spark stops negotiating.

Applying Initial LTV to withdrawals closes the last gap — otherwise a borrower could drain collateral down to the maintenance edge and manufacture the fragile state the ladder exists to prevent.
description: Initial LTV gates issuance and withdrawals, Maintenance LTV triggers the call, Liquidation LTV permits immediate seizure — so curing requires over-correcting past the trigger, not just back under it.
